record._status: BUILT, NOT PUBLISHED. namingFreeze._status still reads AWAITING DANIEL'S APPROVAL.
record._scope: Revert of one paint opacity on Alert, plus a read-only library-wide audit. Exactly one paint was written. No other component, property, variant or node was modified.
record.trigger: checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry.remediation, which was recorded on 2026-08-26 but deliberately not executed in that pass.
record.rootCause: propertySurfaceRepair2026_08_26 assumed Figma MULTIPLIES a bound colour variable's stored alpha by paint.opacity, and therefore read 'variable alpha 0.87 + paint opacity 0.87' as a double application yielding 0.757. Figma does not multiply: it SURFACES the stored alpha into paint.opacity. The two values agreeing is the correct, expected state. Setting opacity to 1 discarded the alpha instead of correcting it.

nodesWritten.name: Text
nodesWritten.note: Binding preserved through the edit - fills was cloned, opacity set, array reassigned.

nodesInspectedButNotWritten.name: Vector (glyph)
nodesInspectedButNotWritten.note: The 2026-08-26 regression had only ever landed on the text node. propertySurfaceRepair2026_08_26 claimed both were changed; only one was. Left untouched rather than rewritten with an identical value.

verification.why: Geometry assertion cannot detect this - the defect is purely a rendering difference. Verified by sampling rendered PNGs.
verification.requestedComparisonUnavailable: A comparison against an adjacent filled severity is not meaningful here: filled/error, filled/info and filled/success all bind color/common/white at stored alpha 1 (white text on saturated fills). No other filled severity uses a sub-1 alpha token, so none reads at the same weight by construction.
verification.referenceUsedInstead: The glyph vector inside the same variant - same variable, same stored alpha, demonstrably never modified.

measurements.textAfter: rgb(33,29,15) - exactly 0.13 x background, the composite for 87% black
measurements.glyphBeforeAndAfter: rgb(54,48,25) - unchanged; matches 0.87 paint x 0.9 Icon-frame opacity = 0.783 effective, predicted rgb(54.7,48.2,25.0)

verification.conclusion: The post-fix text value is the arithmetic result of the restored alpha, not an approximation.

libraryWideAudit.question: Was the same reasoning error applied anywhere else - any node whose paint opacity was forced to 1 while bound to a variable carrying stored alpha?
libraryWideAudit.method: Identified every local COLOR variable whose stored value in any mode has alpha < 1 (17 of 76), then walked every page comparing every fills and strokes paint bound to one of them against that variable's stored alpha. Per-segment text fills read via getStyledTextSegments so mixed-fill TEXT nodes were not skipped.
libraryWideAudit.result: 204 bound-alpha paints, 0 mismatches (counted after the Alert fix; before it, Feedback held the single mismatch).
libraryWideAudit.remoteVariables: 0 paints anywhere in the file bind a non-local variable, so nothing escaped the local-variable list the audit was built from.
libraryWideAudit.touchedComponentsInScope: All five components propertySurfaceRepair2026_08_26 modified were covered - Alert on Feedback; Dialog, Drawer, Menu and Stepper on Surfaces & navigation. Both pages returned clean.
libraryWideAudit.conclusion: Alert's message text 165:53 was the only instance library-wide. The reasoning error was applied once, not repeatedly.
libraryWideAudit.notInScope: This audit compares PAINT-level opacity against bound variable alpha. Node-level opacity is a separate, legitimate mechanism and was not flagged - e.g. Alert's Icon frame 165:49 carries node opacity 0.9, which is MUI's icon treatment and correct.

record.ruleRecorded: standingBatchRules.9_boundPaintAlpha. standingBatchRules.1_instancePaintVerification was also scoped to UNBOUND paints, since its closing sentence read as licence for exactly the change that caused this regression.
